Purpose, prerequisites and stage

Pin engine/toolchain/plugin evidence; establish paths, IDs, documentation and dedicated-server build prerequisites.

Configure current feature

  1. Record installed engine/changelist/compiler/SDK and plugin evidence. Keep source ZIP and license check blocked until the actual private archive is available.
  2. In the separate RPG C++ project create the registered native bootstrap classes, build Development Editor, then create BP_PlayerCharacter, BP_RPGPlayerController, BP_ZoneGameMode and BP_RPGGameInstance.
  3. Set Project Settings > Maps & Modes: BP_RPGGameInstance. L_TerrainLab World Settings > GameMode Override: BP_ZoneGameMode; child Class Defaults controller/pawn point to registered children. Create IA_Move as Axis2D, IA_Cancel as Boolean and the two mapping contexts; no movement implementation is implied yet.

Exact test-world edits

Run now: current-phase integrated scenarios

  1. Save L_TerrainLab with a clear PlayerStart and a blocking dry floor. Do not place an auto-possessed duplicate pawn.
  2. Launch ordinary Play In Editor from PlayerStart. Inspect the effective GameMode, controller and pawn identities and local screen router.
  3. Stop and restart twice; open WBP_Options through the local controller and close with Cancel.
Expected success
Exactly one controller and possessed body are created; no duplicate mapping or menu screen exists.
The native project build result and actual plugin inventory are recorded separately from this documentation.

Explicitly not active yet

  1. Source art audit and PaperZD compatibility are unresolved until supplied/inspected. Full movement begins02; networked identity/economics do not exist in00.

Expected rejection and concurrency results

current-phase fixtureRemove DefaultPawnClass temporarily: spawn validation reports MissingPawnClass; restore it rather than placing an extra pawn.
current-phase fixtureMissing required native parent prevents child creation; do not select an unrelated engine parent to conceal a build failure.

Regression, disconnect and restart

  1. Restart the test environment twice; one admitted pawn per account, one local input context installation, no stale widgets.
  2. Repeat the previous phase success case after all new assignments; definitions missing from this phase must fail closed, not fall back to client saves.
  3. Before networking, verify local cleanup but do not label it a multiplayer test.

Stop condition and deferred work

Installation record, source provenance, plugin gate and a blank C++ project created by the developer.

Stop on a failed required assertion, missing required rule definition, duplicate authority or unverified dependency that this phase relies on. Legal debug art may support physics tests but cannot close the archive/PaperZD art gate. Do not activate future-phase systems merely because their full-game chapter exists.
